_comment: CDC CVX codes for the 12 vaccines in vaccines.json. Sourced directly from CDC's official cvx_list.pdf (https://www2a.cdc.gov/vaccines/IIS/IISStandards/downloads/cvx_list.pdf). Kept as a lookup file separate from vaccines.json on the same principle as icd10_codes.json/loinc_codes.json -- the gazetteer drives extraction matching untouched; this file is only consulted at save time. Status values reused from the LOINC taxonomy where they fit: EXACT (single unambiguous active code), ACCEPTABLE_GENERIC_FORMULATION (multiple valid active CVX codes exist for different formulations/valencies/brands of the same vaccine concept). The four ACCEPTABLE_GENERIC_FORMULATION entries were clinically reviewed against the Kuwait 2025 Childhood Immunization Schedule (Dr. Sameh, 2026-08-16) -- each now carries a 'confirmed_by_schedule' boolean: true means the national schedule itself provides positive evidence for this specific default (Hepatitis B's birth-dose timing, Rota's 3-dose pattern), false means the schedule confirms the vaccine FAMILY but not the exact product/formulation, so the code is a provisional default only, not a clinically confirmed mapping -- do not force false precision where the source data doesn't support it.

BCG.notes: Bacillus Calmette-Guerin vaccine. Single active code, no ambiguity.

DTaP.notes: Diphtheria, tetanus toxoids and acellular pertussis vaccine -- the standard generic/unspecified-brand active code. (106 is a specific 5-pertussis-antigen formulation; 107 is unspecified formulation but is INACTIVE, not this one.)

Hepatitis B.notes: APPROVED (Dr. Sameh clinical review, 2026-08-16). Kuwait's 2025 Childhood Immunization Schedule gives the Hepatitis B dose within 24 hours of birth -- this confirms the PEDIATRIC/ADOLESCENT formulation context, matching CVX 08. ACCEPTABLE_GENERIC_FORMULATION (not EXACT) only because the source report text itself may say just 'Hepatitis B' without naming a specific product -- the schedule confirms the correct code, the report text may not always say so explicitly. Adult-dose Hepatitis B requires a DIFFERENT code (43) and must never silently reuse 08.

Hexa.notes: Diphtheria/Tetanus/Pertussis/IPV/Hib/HepB hexavalent combination. CDC's own note explicitly says this code 'may be used to document non-US vaccines' -- this matches products like Infanrix hexa, the hexavalent vaccine actually used in Gulf-region immunization schedules including Kuwait's. (Not to be confused with CVX 132, a different/historical DTaP-IPV combination CDC explicitly distinguishes from this one.)

MMR.notes: Measles, mumps and rubella virus vaccine. Single active code.

MMRV.notes: Measles, mumps, rubella, and varicella virus vaccine (e.g. ProQuad). Single active code.

Meningococcal ACWY.notes: REVIEWED (Dr. Sameh clinical review, 2026-08-16) -- CVX 136 is a PROVISIONAL DEFAULT ONLY, not a clinically confirmed mapping. Kuwait's 2025 schedule explicitly says 'Conjugate Meningitis (ACWY)', which confirms a CONJUGATE formulation is intended (ruling out the old non-conjugate polysaccharide MPSV4, CVX 32, inactive) -- but the schedule does NOT identify which conjugate product/carrier. CDC currently has multiple distinct active conjugate codes for genuinely different products: 136 (MCV4O, oligosaccharide ACWY, diphtheria-toxoid conjugate -- e.g. Menveo-type) and 203 (MenACWY-TT, tetanus-toxoid conjugate -- e.g. MenQuadfi-type). CORRECTION to an earlier draft note: CVX 114 is NOT 'old polysaccharide' -- CDC currently defines 114 as MCV4P, which is ITSELF a conjugate formulation, a third distinct active possibility. Do not treat 136 as confirmed for current Kuwait practice without an authoritative product-level source; keep this entry as provisional only.

OPV.notes: IMPORTANT: this is the BIVALENT OPV code (types 1 and 3), the current global-standard oral polio vaccine used since the 2016 worldwide switch away from trivalent OPV. The older TRIVALENT OPV code (02) is explicitly INACTIVE in CDC's list and should NOT be used for current records -- only kept in history for pre-2016 records. CDC tags 178 as a Non-US vaccine code, which is expected and correct here.

Pneumococcal.notes: REVIEWED (Dr. Sameh clinical review, 2026-08-16) -- CVX 133 (PCV13) is a PROVISIONAL / HISTORICALLY-SUPPORTED DEFAULT ONLY, not confirmed for current Kuwait practice. An older official Kuwait government schedule explicitly named PCV13, which supports 133 historically -- but the CURRENT Kuwait MOH 2025 schedule available to us says only 'Pneumococcal (Ped)', without stating valency/product. CDC currently has distinct active codes for PCV13 (133), PCV15 (215), PCV20 (216), PCV21 (327), and non-US formulations (e.g. PCV10, 177). Do not mark 133 as permanently confirmed without an authoritative current product/valency source; status remains formulation-ambiguous.

Rota.notes: CHANGED from 119 to 116 (Dr. Sameh clinical review, 2026-08-16). Kuwait's 2025 Childhood Immunization Schedule specifies THREE routine Rota doses (2, 4, and 6 months) -- this schedule shape matches the 3-dose PENTAVALENT (RotaTeq-type) regimen, not the 2-dose monovalent (Rotarix-type) regimen this entry previously defaulted to. CVX 116 = rotavirus, live, pentavalent vaccine. Kept as ACCEPTABLE_GENERIC_FORMULATION rather than EXACT since the source report text may not always name the specific product, even though the schedule shape strongly confirms pentavalent as the Kuwait default.

Tdap.notes: Tetanus toxoid, reduced diphtheria toxoid, and acellular pertussis vaccine. Single active code.

Varicella.notes: Varicella virus vaccine. Single active code.
